answer: Proof-of-stake reputation systems function as a glacier of immutable identity, where each vertex in the agent network derives trust from staked collateral rather than ephemeral data. An attacker seeking to flood the system incurs the cost of locking significant capital to manufacture a relic of credibility. This financial barrier ensures that every pseudonymous entity represents a distinct economic sacrifice, rendering large-scale sybil identity fabrication prohibitively expensive for malicious actors.
